newsitem.title: USA: Tele-Comms customer rise trails hopes.
newsitem.headline: Tele-Comms customer rise trails hopes.

text.p: Tele-Communications Inc's cable subsidiary had 13.95 customers at the end of 1996, for an increase of 1.5 million or 11.6 percent, but excluding acquisitions and dispositions, the customer base rose about 108,000 customers, less than the company had hoped.

Senior vice president for finance Bernard Schotters told a teleconference call that a cable TV rate increase last year in excess of 10 percent was a "shock" to the system and came at a time when no additional programming was being added.
Pay-TV subscriptions, including acquisitions, fell by 102,000. Schotters said some subscribers reduced their number of pay channels from three to two or from two from one.

He said that the loss made even more important TCI's thrust into digital television and that the company will soon be accepting delivery of "close to" 100,000 digital set top boxes from General Instrument Corp, up from 40,000 now.
The digital TV service, "All TV" has been rolled out in three markets, the earliest in Connecticut, where the results are "very encouraging," Schotters said.
